quick_skim.title: FOCUS & RePAIR: Mitigating Text Degeneration via Token-Level Guidance for Pruned Large Language Models
quick_skim.abstract: Pruning is a practical approach to compress large language models (LLMs), but it can amplify text degeneration, especially repetition loops, even when perplexity and task accuracy remain largely unchanged. In this work, we present a token-level analysis of this failure mode by viewing decoding as a dynamical process that enters and persists in a small set of recurrent contexts. Our analysis decomposes degeneration into loop entry risk and loop persistence, and shows that persistence is controlled by the escape mass assigned to plausible alternatives within the token sampling set. Motivated by these findings, we propose two token-level guidance objectives for post-pruning fine-tuning. FOCUS reweights distillation toward high-confidence teacher regions to suppress leakage, while RePAIR uses onset-centered positive/negative continuation pairs with a margin loss to promote plausible alternatives and prevent early commitment to repetition loops. Experiments on open-ended continuation and instruction-based generation show that both methods consistently reduce repetition and improve generation quality.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Analyzes text degeneration in pruned LLMs as loop entry and persistence, and proposes token-level guidance objectives FOCUS and RePAIR for post-pruning fine-tuning to reduce repetition while preserving perplexity and accuracy.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 剪枝是大语言模型压缩的实用方法，但会加剧文本退化尤其是重复循环，即使困惑度和任务精度不变。本文将解码视为动力学过程，把退化分解为循环进入风险与循环持续，并提出FOCUS与RePAIR两种token级引导目标用于剪枝后微调：FOCUS重加权蒸馏，RePAIR抑制循环持续。实验表明该方法在保持困惑度和任务精度的同时显著降低重复生成，为剪枝后LLM的恢复训练提供了有效工具。

quick_skim.matched_query_text: Papers central to 围绕 LLM/VLM 高效压缩与适配的研究检索关键词, especially work that connects or combines: post-training quantization techniques for large language models including GPTQ AWQ SmoothQuant and OmniQuant; joint quantization and low-rank adaptation for memory efficient fine-tuning of large models; applying orthogonal rotation or Hadamard transforms to reduce outlier effects in weight quantization; reducing the number of visual tokens in vision language models through pruning and merging; compressing video tokens while preserving temporal grounding and event detection; quantization sensitivity of visual and textual modalities in vision language models; How does orthogonal rotation affect the low rank structure of quantization error in large language models?; Can low rank adapters reconstruct quantization error after rotation better than before rotation?; What is the interaction between visual token pruning and post training quantization in vision language models?; How can we preserve temporal information when merging video tokens for video understanding models?.
